title: Mezzrow, the Bechet dispute and the Moulin Rouge acts
summary: Moore describes Mezzrow in Paris, a money dispute with Bechet, and eating with two Moulin Rouge performers.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: How about Mezzrow? You performed with him.

Mezzrow lived in Paris. He put down America, he loved Paris. He's got his finger in every pot there. I remember one time there was a hassle between Sidney Bechet and Mezz Mezzrow concerning contracts and payments of moneys pertaining to records. Sidney used to tell me, 'You see that man, he better give me my money cause I made them records too.' But I couldn't get in the middle between those two because I didn't know what was happening, it's not my business. But between the two guys, they're friends but still have their business tangled up in certain ways like the moneys on the records.
Yeah, they teamed up for some recording dates in the late '40s.

And there was another man, a trumpet player by the name of Jack Butler, we called him Jacques, like the French Jacques. Then there was another act there at the Moulin Rouge, Paterson and Jackson, two big guys. I used to hang around with them. We used to eat together because I love to eat and they liked to eat, I didn't want to be alone. Any Frenchman doesn't eat as much as I, but Pork Chop,
